resources.string: Unofficial, experimental screen reader with NVDA\'s sounds, wording and Python console

Nvidiator is an unofficial, experimental screen reader that brings NVDA's sounds, wording, translations and Python console to Android. It is not made or endorsed by NV Access.

Before you turn it on: the accessibility shortcut (hold both volume keys) still works while Nvidiator is on, so you can always turn TalkBack back on. If no speech starts within 15 seconds, Nvidiator turns itself off.

Nvidiator can read everything on the screen and perform actions for you, like any screen reader.

An unofficial, experimental port of NVDA\'s sound and soul to Android: NVDA\'s sounds and beeps, NVDA\'s wording in NVDA\'s own translations, NVDA\'s gestures and keyboard commands, and NVDA\'s Python console. Not made or endorsed by NV Access.
Nvidiator is off. Turn it on in Accessibility settings, under Installed apps or Downloaded apps.

This is an experiment. Some apps may not read well.

• Your way back: hold both volume keys for 3 seconds to use the accessibility shortcut. Nvidiator never takes over the volume keys, so the shortcut always works. Set the shortcut to TalkBack first, in Accessibility settings.
• If no speech starts within 15 seconds of turning Nvidiator on, it plays NVDA's error sound and turns itself off.
• To exit, open the NVDA menu (swipe down then right, or tap with three fingers) and choose Exit, or press NVDA+Q twice on a keyboard.
• Turn TalkBack off when Nvidiator is on. Two screen readers at once fight over every touch.

To switch between TalkBack and Nvidiator in one step, give Nvidiator this permission once from a computer:\nadb shell pm grant com.irondonkey.nvidiator android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS\nWithout it, Exit turns Nvidiator off and you turn TalkBack on with the accessibility shortcut (hold both volume keys).
The switching permission is granted. In the NVDA menu, Exit then Exit to TalkBack turns Nvidiator off and TalkBack on in one step.

A short tour of Nvidiator\'s gestures. They follow NVDA\'s touch commands, with TalkBack\'s gestures for the Android buttons.

string-array.name: tutorial_steps
string-array.item: Explore: slide one finger around the screen to hear what is under it. Double tap anywhere to activate the last item you heard.
Move: swipe right for the next object and left for the previous one. Swipe up to move to the object containing it, and down to move to the first object inside it.
Text: swipe up then down to switch between object mode and text mode. In text mode, swipe right or left for characters, up or down for lines, and swipe right or left with three fingers for words.
Read: swipe down then up, or swipe down with three fingers, to read from here to the end of the screen. Tap with two fingers to stop speech.
The NVDA menu: swipe down then right, tap with three fingers, or double tap with two fingers. It has Preferences, Tools, Help and Exit.
Android buttons: swipe down then left for Back, up then left for Home, left then up for Recent apps, and right then down for notifications.
Input help: tap with four fingers to turn it on. Each gesture then says what it does instead of doing it. Tap with four fingers again to turn it off.
Keyboard: Insert or Caps Lock is the NVDA key. NVDA+N opens the menu, NVDA+Down arrow reads all, NVDA+T reads the title and NVDA+1 turns input help on.
Getting out: choose Exit in the NVDA menu, or press NVDA+Q twice. The accessibility shortcut (hold both volume keys) always works too.

resources.string: Turn input help on, then try any gesture to hear what it does. Tap with four fingers to turn input help off again.
